Maximizing Apparent Velocity in a Camera's Frame

How should a drone move to maximize its apparent velocity in the frame of a camera? This Demonstration solves this problem for a drone that can move a distance r in any direction.

Details

If a drone (represented as a particle) can move with equal velocity in any direction, the set of possible 3D coordinates after one time step is a 3D sphere. The image plane of a camera projects all 3D points into a 2D camera frame [1]. If the sphere is centered at (xc, yc, zc) with radius r and camera focal length λ, then the optimal goal location (x, y, z) for the drone is parameterized by the (latitude, longitude) pair (ϕ, θ):

ϕ = 3π⁄2 − arctan(√r2, √xc2 + yc2 + zc2 − r2) + arctan(√xc2 + yc2, zc),

θ = arctan(xc, yc).

If (xc, yc) is (0, 0), there are infinite solutions with θ ∈ [0, 360]°.

The goal location is:

x = xc + r cos θ sin ϕ

y = yc + r sin θ sin ϕ

z = zc + r cos ϕ

This projects onto the image plane at the point λ⁄z(x, y). Because cos ϕ is always negative, the drone decreases the distance in z. Interestingly, the sphere projects into a 2D ellipse in the image plane. With equations given by [2], the ellipse is centered at

(x λ⁄z − r λ √(xc2 + yc2 + zc2 − r2)/(r2 − zc2)2 cos(arctan(y⁄x)), y λ⁄z − r λ √(xc2 + yc2 + zc2 − r2)/(r2 − zc2)2 sin(arctan(y⁄x))),

with

major axis = r λ √(xc2 + yc2 + zc2 − r2)/(r2 − zc2)2,

minor axis = r λ⁄√r2 − zc2

and

ellipse rotation angle = arctan(y⁄x).

The focal length λ is 5 in this Demonstration.

References
[1] M. W. Spong, S. Hutchinson and M. Vidyasagar, Robot Modeling and Control, Hoboken, NJ: John Wiley and Sons, 2006.
[2] D. Eberly. "Perspective Projection of an Ellipsoid." (Oct 30, 2018) www.geometrictools.com/Documentation/PerspectiveProjectionEllipsoid.pdf.
